paper_sections.title: Neural correlates of metacognitive systematic bias
The different cognitive mechanisms between overestimated bias and underestimated bias
Dissociable neural networks supporting metacognitive systematic bias

description.value: The study used event-related fMRI, univariate GLM, multivariate pattern analysis, and effective connectivity analyses to investigate neural mechanisms of overestimated and underestimated metacognitive systematic bias during encoding and immediate judgments of learning for word pairs.

spans.text: This study utilized the fMRI technique, combining univariate analysis methods with multivariate pattern analysis, to observe the neural patterns of systematic bias and clarify the mechanisms of overestimated bias or underestimated bias.

value: The monitoring dual-memories hypothesis and memory strength hypothesis offer partial explanations for systematic biases in metacognitive monitoring.
The study hypothesized that working memory and metacognitive monitoring regions would contribute to the formation of overestimated and underestimated metacognitive biases.

spans.text: The monitoring dual-memories hypothesis and memory strength hypothesis offer partial explanations for systematic biases in metacognitive monitoring.

description.value: fMRI preprocessing included DICOM-to-NIfTI conversion, discarding the first three images of each run, slice-timing correction, realignment for head motion, coregistration to structural images, normalization to the Montreal Neurological Institute template, resampling to 3 × 3 × 3 mm voxels, and spatial smoothing.

spans.text: First, all the EPI DICOM data were converted to NIFTI format. The first three images from each run were automatically discarded by the scanner to allow scanner equilibrium. Second, all volume slice scan times were corrected to the middle time slice and realigned to the first scan to correct for head motion. Third, the structural images of each subject were coregistered with the mean functional images, and then the images were normalized to the Montreal Neurological Institute template. Fourth, all voxels were resampled to 3 × 3 × 3 mm. Last, all functional volumes were smoothed by using an 8-mm FWHM isotropic Gaussian kernel.

name.value: encoding and immediate judgments of learning task

spans.text: In the scanner and each run, participants performed an encoding and immediate judgment of learning (JOLs) task.

description.value: Participants encoded abstract word pairs and immediately judged how likely they were to remember the unseen target in a later recognition test. During the encoding-JOL phase, participants viewed a cue word and predicted subsequent memory performance using a four-point scale.

spans.text: After encoding each pair, participants saw one word from the pair (the cue) on the screen and were asked to predict how likely they would remember the unseen target in the post-scan recognition task on a four-point scale
JOLs magnitude was high ("will remember" prediction) but was later failed to recognize in the post-scan recognition test (JOL M ), which is overestimated bias.
